source_text: Inde dilectionem iam tecum suam Dominus initiata caritate firmauit, inde amicitiam tecum quam discipulis suis sub triumpho crucis suae tradidit dedicauitque dicens: si feceritis quae mando uobis, iam non dicam seruos uos sed amicos, inde martyrium, inde sacerdotii electionem signauit. amicitia est, per quam ad Christi uultus admitteris, extraordinaria hostia peruenire. sic eliguntur iusti, sic probantur religiosi ac simplices in Christi timore electi, ut ante remunerationi fidei destineris, ante praemio deuotae mentis in Domino dignus habearis, quam uenerit hora decreti, quam exceperis sententiam Christi, probatam te et paratam hostiam electio caelestis inueniat. etenim ille te qui non mendax est Deus, qui episcopum plebi suae de improuiso constituit, ille plena dilectione suae uoluntatis te coronabit. tantum tunc ut nostri memineris petimus et oramus, cum pudicitia t adlectionis Domini probata atque immaculata hostia ante Christi tribunal adstiteris, cum gloriam gratiae Dei praemio deuotae mentis ac remunerationem exceperis, memoriter haereat et tenaciter sensibus tuis maneat quam nobis impertire dignaris dilectio caritatis: ut orationibus tuis peccata nostra uel ueniam consequantur, ut meritis iustitiae tuae uitae nostrae delicta purgentur. etenim martyrii instar esse confido, peccatorem iusti martyris petitione meruisse saluari, et ut cum ipse pro te promouere quid precibus tuis minus possis martyris meritis libereris. sic Iob iustus pro amicorum trium peccatis a Deo rogaturus et impetraturus ostenditur, et probatio timoris eius et fidei Domini uoce teste signatur. cum ergo in die liberationis tuae, carissime, repraesentare te Christi uultibus coeperis, cum in aeternitatem perpetuitatemque uiuendi regnare cum Christo felici sorte successeris, pro Domini misericordia in mente me habe Celsum puerum tuum, sanctissime.
thought_title: The bond of friendship and the coming crown
orientation: The author is addressing Vigilius, the newly elected bishop, about the friendship Christ has established with him and the martyrdom and reward that await him.
pass_a_gloss: From there the Lord has already strengthened his love with you by an initiated affection, from there he has dedicated and consecrated the friendship with you which he handed over to his disciples under the triumph of his cross, saying: if you do what I command you, I will no longer call you servants but friends, from there he has marked the martyrdom, from there the election of the priesthood. It is friendship, through which you are admitted to the face of Christ, to arrive as an extraordinary sacrifice. Thus the righteous are chosen, thus the devout and simple are approved, chosen in the fear of Christ, so that you are destined for the reward of faith before, you are held worthy of the prize of a devoted mind in the Lord before, than the hour of the decree comes, than you receive the sentence of Christ, so that the heavenly election may find you a tested and prepared sacrifice. For he who is God, who is not a liar, who appointed a bishop for his people unexpectedly, he will crown you with the full love of his will. Only then we ask and pray that you remember us, when you stand before the tribunal of Christ as a sacrifice tested and immaculate by the chastity of the Lord's choosing, when you receive the glory of God's grace as the prize of a devoted mind and the recompense, may the love of affection which you deign to share with us remain memorably fixed and tenaciously in your thoughts: so that by your prayers our sins may obtain pardon, so that by the merits of your righteousness the offenses of our life may be purged. For I am confident that it is the likeness of martyrdom, that a sinner has deserved to be saved by the petition of a righteous martyr, and that when you yourself can do less for yourself by your prayers, you are freed by the merits of a martyr. Thus righteous Job is shown as one who will ask and obtain from God for the sins of his three friends, and the proof of his fear and faith is marked by the voice of the Lord as witness. Therefore when on the day of your liberation, dearest one, you begin to present yourself to the face of Christ, when you succeed in reigning with Christ in eternity and perpetuity of living by a happy lot, for the mercy of the Lord have me in mind, and Celsus your boy, most holy one.

choices.why: Keeps the passive participle force of initiata and the instrumental sense of caritate; 'initiated' preserves the idea of a love that has been begun or inaugurated.
rejected: by a love that has been started

choices.english: under the triumph of his cross
choices.why: Literal rendering of sub with the ablative; 'triumph' is the standard English for triumphus and fits the military metaphor.
rejected: beneath the victory of his cross
in the triumph of his cross

choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun order and the literal sense of extraordinaria as 'outside the ordinary course'; hostia is rendered 'sacrifice' as the victim offered.
Dative of purpose rendered with 'for'; remuneratio is 'reward' or 'recompense', and fidei is objective genitive.

choices.english: you as a tested and prepared sacrifice
choices.why: Keeps the predicative participles modifying te; 'tested' for probatam and 'prepared' for paratam preserve the passive sense.
rejected: you, a proven and ready victim
you as an approved and made-ready offering

choices.why: Instar with genitive means 'the equivalent of' or 'like'; 'likeness' captures the idea that being saved by a martyr's prayer is comparable to martyrdom itself.

bible_refs.note: si feceritis quae mando uobis, iam non dicam seruos uos sed amicos
sic Iob iustus pro amicorum trium peccatis a Deo rogaturus et impetraturus ostenditur

pass_b_english: From that moment the Lord, having begun his love for you, made it firm; from that moment he sealed the friendship he handed over and dedicated to his disciples under the triumph of his cross, saying: “If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants but friends” (John 15:14-15); from that moment he sealed your martyrdom and your election to the priesthood. It is friendship through which you are admitted to the face of Christ, to arrive as an extraordinary sacrifice. This is how the righteous are chosen, this is how the devout and simple are approved, chosen in the fear of Christ, so that you are destined for the reward of faith before the hour of decision comes, so that you are held worthy in the Lord of the prize of a devoted mind before you receive Christ’s sentence, so that the heavenly election finds you a tested and prepared sacrifice. For he who is not a liar, God, who unexpectedly made you bishop for his people, he will crown you with the full love of his will. Only then we ask and pray that you remember us, when you stand before the tribunal of Christ as a sacrifice approved and spotless in the chastity of the Lord’s choosing, when you receive the glory of God’s grace as the prize of a devoted mind and as your recompense; let the love of charity you deign to share with us remain fixed in your memory and cling to your thoughts, so that by your prayers our sins may obtain pardon, so that by the merits of your righteousness the offenses of our life may be cleansed. For I am confident that it is the likeness of martyrdom for a sinner to deserve salvation by the petition of a righteous martyr, and that when you can do little for yourself by your prayers, you are set free by the merits of a martyr. Thus righteous Job is shown about to pray to God for the sins of his three friends and to obtain it, and the proof of his fear and faith is marked by the Lord’s own voice as witness. Therefore, dearest one, when on the day of your liberation you begin to present yourself before the face of Christ, when you pass into eternity and the endlessness of living to reign with Christ by a happy lot, for the Lord’s mercy keep me in mind, and Celsus your boy, most holy one.
notes: The text 'cum pudicitia t adlectionis Domini' appears to have a stray 't' after 'pudicitia'; it is likely a scribal error or OCR artifact. The gloss treats it as 'cum pudicitia adlectionis Domini' (with the chastity of the Lord's choosing).
